question: In a quadrilateral EFGH, ∠E = 52° and ∠F = 37°. The bisectors of ∠G and ∠H meet at X. What is the measure of ∠HXG?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In any quadrilateral, the angle formed by the intersection of the angle bisectors of two adjacent angles is half the sum of the remaining two interior angles.

⇒ ∠HXG = (∠E + ∠F) ÷ 2

⇒ ∠HXG = (52° + 37°) ÷ 2

⇒ ∠HXG = 89° ÷ 2 = 44.5°

**∴ The correct answer is 44.5°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

∠E = 52°

∠F = 37°

X is the intersection point of the angle bisectors of ∠G and ∠H.

**Formula Used:**

Sum of all interior angles of a quadrilateral = 360°

Sum of all interior angles of a triangle = 180°

**Calculations:**

In quadrilateral EFGH,

⇒ ∠E + ∠F + ∠G + ∠H = 360°

⇒ 52° + 37° + ∠G + ∠H = 360°

⇒ 89° + ∠G + ∠H = 360°

⇒ ∠G + ∠H = 360° − 89°

⇒ ∠G + ∠H = 271°

Since XG and XH are the respective angle bisectors of ∠G and ∠H,

⇒ ∠HGX = ∠G ÷ 2

⇒ ∠GHX = ∠H ÷ 2

Now, considering triangle HXG,

⇒ ∠HXG + ∠HGX + ∠GHX = 180°

⇒ ∠HXG + (∠G ÷ 2) + (∠H ÷ 2) = 180°

⇒ ∠HXG + (∠G + ∠H) ÷ 2 = 180°

⇒ ∠HXG + (271° ÷ 2) = 180°

⇒ ∠HXG + 135.5° = 180°

⇒ ∠HXG = 180° − 135.5°

⇒ ∠HXG = 44.5°

**∴ The correct answer is 44.5°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle Sum Property of a Quadrilateral

The sum of the interior angles of any simple quadrilateral is always 360°. This fundamental property applies because a quadrilateral can be divided into two separate triangles along a diagonal.

Incentre of a Triangle

When the angle bisectors of the two base angles of a triangle intersect at a point (the incentre), the angle formed at the intersection is equal to 90° + (∠opposite base angle ÷ 2).

Cyclic Quadrilateral Property

A cyclic quadrilateral is one in which all four vertices lie precisely on the circumference of a single circle. In such a shape, the sum of any pair of opposite interior angles is strictly supplementary (adding to 180°).
